paid_market_gaps.gap: File-server behavior detection (Varonis, Netwrix, Superna) is quote-only, enterprise-priced; little for 1-3 server shops
Storage-native detection locked to specific enterprise NAS platforms and multi-year capacity contracts
Deception/canary detection costly for small teams; median Thinkst Canary deal about $9,900/year
Endpoint anti-ransomware on file shares produces false positives blocking legitimate writes (e.g. AutoCAD exports)

wtp_evidence: Established paid backup and file-security products with public per-device and per-server prices (Acronis, Veeam, ManageEngine) sell widely; enterprise buyers pay large sums for Varonis.
bundling_note: Microsoft Defender for Business ($3/user/month, servers add-on) includes ransomware attack disruption, and Synology DSM offers immutable snapshots with ransomware-triggered snapshots.
summary: Crowded: backup vendors, EDR and enterprise file-security platforms all cover it, and Microsoft/NAS vendors bundle protection. Only narrow opening: cheap, low-false-positive file-share canary detection plus guided restore for 1-3 server SMBs or MSPs.
